hints.title: Asymmetry of People versus Hat Counts
hints.text: At most ten people exist, while up to forty hats are available. Assigning hats to people one by one inverts the problem into a much smaller state space.

hints.title: Hat Assignment Options Invariant
hints.text: Each hat from 1 to 40 can either be assigned to at most one person who likes it, or skipped altogether.

hints.title: Inverted Mask Iteration Procedure
hints.text: Construct an adjacency list from hat ID to people who desire it. Initialize an array of size 2^n with dp[0] = 1. Process each hat sequentially: for each person who likes the hat, transition backwards from (1 << n) - 1 to 0, adding ways to next state modulo 10^9 + 7. Return dp[(1 << n) - 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(H * N * 2^N) time and O(2^N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Assigning hats to people directly explores 40^10 configurations, which is far too large.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterating over 40 hats with a 2^n person bitmask runs in O(40 * n * 2^n) time using O(2^n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that n <= 10 makes the people subset suitable for a bitmask, prompting an inverted hat-to-person iteration.
